welcomeText: Archmage Thalindra. Avalon sits on a confluence of old ley lines - it's why I teach the high arts here and nowhere else on this coast. Name a school - fire, water, earth, air, dark or light - and I'll show you what it holds.

topics.response: Veilstone Aegis, Wellspring Mercy, Leyward Bastion, Dawnwell Renewal, Sanctum Ward - the ley-line wards and mercies. For the killing arts, name a school: fire, water, earth, air, dark or light.
The Wilds' fey draw on the same ley lines I do, gentler than my own working. That kinship is the only reason they still tolerate a tower full of spellbooks in their woods.

The high arts were never meant to be taught lightly. Every school offers the same six rungs - at the hundred-and-fiftieth level, then every fifty levels after, up to the four hundredth - and each rung demands a mind to match it. Come back when you're ready.
The apex of every school is the same distance up the ladder: the four hundredth level, and a mind of a thousand in its governing art. Name a school and I'll show you the whole climb.
Scorchbrand, Pyreburst, Magmaheart Lance, Sunforge Brand, Emberqueen's Wrath, Ashfall - the pyromancer's ladder. Fire answers to Intelligence.
Rime Lance, Frostgale, Abyssal Spear, Tidebreaker, Drowning Deep, Cataclysm's Herald - the tidecaller's ladder. Water answers to Intelligence.
Stonefang, Land Slide, Gravebreaker, Mountain's Fist, Worldroot Upheaval, Tectonic Ruin - the geomancer's ladder. Earth answers to Wisdom.
Galespike, Thunderhead, Skysplitter, Tempest Lance, Stormcaller's Judgment, Heavenfall - the windweaver's ladder. The storm asks for Intelligence and Wisdom in equal measure.
Nightfang, Shadowblight, Soulrend, Voidreave Lance, Umbral Tide, Eclipse of Ruin - the shadowmancer's ladder. Darkness answers to Intelligence.
Sunscour, Dawnflare, Radiant Spear, Seraph's Verdict, Hallowed Nova, Solar Apotheosis - the lightbringer's ladder. Light answers to Wisdom.

Every master of a school should wear its colors. Ember red, tide blue, verdant green, storm gold, shadow black, dawn white - woven on the ley lines themselves, and they will only settle on the shoulders of a caster of real standing.

welcomeText: The crossing to Kraanhold isn't a pleasant one. Clear the road trolls harassing the coast first, and I'll see you safely across.

topics.response: Trolls have been working the coast road east of here for longer than I've kept this dock. Thin their numbers and I'll take you across to Kraanhold myself - can't risk the boat with them still raiding the shore.
Kraanhold. A stretch of coast and mountain out past the shoals - centaurs hold the marches, and it only gets worse from there. Drakes, they say, further up in the peaks.
Nothing clever about them, just big and mean. They've gotten bold enough to block the coast road entirely some days.
Watch the tide line. I've lost more than one boat to trolls wading out after it.

welcomeText: Welcome, traveler. I am Elder Ophira of Avalon Sanctuary. You stand at the seam between two halves of one isle - ask, and I will tell you of our plight.

topics.response: The Avalon Wilds still answer to the old pact. The fey there remain loyal, the groves unmarred - for now. That could change before the season turns.
South of here spreads the Fading Veil - a blight eating outward from Ysolde's lair. Every season it claims more ground. We do not know how to stop it.
Sir Caradoc was once the truest knight our isle ever raised. Ysolde bound his spirit to her service when he fell defending the old borders. What walks the Veil now wears his armor, not his honor.
Ysolde was no matriarch of ours. She came veiled, in peace, and left the corruption that now bears her name. She is the source of the blight, not merely its steward.
The Verdant Warden is the last of the old treant guardians still standing his ground against the blight. He answers to no one, not even us - but he has not fallen, and that alone gives us hope.
I have work for capable hands - ask me of the Wilds if you'd stand vigil with our loyal fey, or of the Veil if you'd push back its corruption.

welcomeText: Few make it this far and fewer still make it back. What do you need, champion?

topics.response: The Bastion Wardens have held that ruin for longer than anyone living remembers. Break enough of them and the old wards will finally weaken.
The Greater Drake sleeps at the bastion's heart. Every warden that falls is one less reason for it to stay asleep. Think on that before you wake it.
May whatever you worship still be listening where you're going.

welcomeText: Welcome to what's left of the dock. Nobody sails from here anymore - not since the reavers took the shore and Ithrak took their coin.

topics.response: Coastwarden Ithrak runs the reavers squatting on the shore south of here, and he's the only one left who knows the safe line through the shoal to Avalon. Clear his warband, take his chart off his corpse, and bring it to me - I'll see you're recognized as someone Avalon can trust.
Ithrak used to be a knight, they say, before he decided guarding a smuggling route paid better than guarding anything worth guarding.
Avalon's out there, past the shoal. Nobody's crossed it on their own in years - not without that chart, or without knowing the tide by heart the way Ithrak did.
Watch the tideline past the dock. The reavers don't wait for you to see them first.
My boy tried the crossing years back, chart or no chart. The tide took him before the reavers ever did. I don't sail anymore. I just make sure nobody else goes in as blind as he did.

The fey pact's older than this dock, older than Ithrak's smuggling. Sailors used to say it was fraying even before the reavers came. I don't know what's true and what's dockside talk - only that fewer of us who cross ever come back to say.

welcomeText: Careful where you step. Something's been dragging people under since the tide turned.

topics.response: Deep Ones have been dragging travelers under all along this stretch of the coast. Thin their numbers and I'll see you paid for it.
There's a bigger one down there. The others answer to it. I wouldn't go looking for it without help.
Stay off the wet ground after dark. That's when they surface.

welcomeText: The centaur warbands have been raiding out of the western marches again. Windhowl needs sellswords, not just soldiers.

topics.response: Centaur Warriors have been raiding the marches west of here, and their king rides with them now. Thin their ranks and Windhowl will pay you well for it.
Their king wears a crown he has no right to. Bring me his head and I'll see you rewarded beyond the usual bounty.
Resha still carries bows blessed for centaur-slaying, if the old stories are true. Ask her, not me.
Watch the tall grass. They ambush from it.

welcomeText: Halvard. Windhowl's roads aren't as safe as they look - prove you can clear them before you go wandering the hills.

topics.response: Brigands have been working the roads north and east of town again, bolder than usual. Clear enough of them out and I'll know you can hold a line before you go looking for whatever's smoldering in those hills south of here.
South of here the hills catch fire on their own some nights - Cinderreach, we call it. A drake's made a den of it, or so the hunters who came back say.
Windhowl doesn't send its own out past the marches without knowing they can fight. The centaurs further out taught us that the hard way.
Deserters and opportunists, mostly. Nothing organized, just enough of them to make the roads dangerous for anyone traveling alone.

welcomeText: Turn back if you're not ready. What's past this ridge doesn't forgive.

topics.response: Kraanian Dragonguard hold the approach to the old drakes' lair, further out than anything we've mapped before. Cull enough of them and the Vigil will pay you well.
Something older than the Greater Drake sleeps past the guard line. The maps just call it the Arch Drake. I hope they're wrong.
Don't go past the guard line alone. I mean that as a warning, not a dare.

welcomeText: Quartermaster Elenna, at your service. If you mean to walk the Wilds or the Veil, you'll want better steel than you're carrying.

topics.response: Everything on this rack was forged or bought for Sanctuary's own garrison. It'll serve you just as well out there.
We hold this seam between the Wilds and the Veil. Lose the Sanctuary and both halves of the isle lose their only safe ground.
The Wilds are gentler than the Veil, but don't let that fool you - a Moonlit Stalker will still take your arm off.

welcomeText: Sorry, we're closed during the night and I'm off to bed.

topics.response: The name is Rhodar Heatforge but people usually call me Rhodar.
Yes, that's my name.
I am the weaponsmith of the village. I forge all my weapons myself from ore obtained in the mountains.
You want to buy something, is that it?

Wait a minute! Lemme see that hammer you have... hey, that's mine!!! How did you find it?! Ah.. Qardos.. that wretched blackguard... of course! If I was a bit younger, I swear I'd put this hammer to good use. Now, will you give it back to me?

Hey, you've killed %u goblins, right? Looks like you hate them as much as I do. Come with me in the back of the store, I've got something to show you that might be useful. Look at this beautiful sword, it's a Goblin Slayer sword. It has the uncanny ability of literally destroying goblins. It's yours if you're willing to pay the fair price of 25000 gold pieces. Does that sound fair to you?
The desert of "Vulture's" "Den" is nearly as hot as my forge. You shouldn't go there or I'll lose yet another good customer.
That's the name of the desert on the west part of the island.
What do you want to sell?
I would not go there if I were you. Unless you're wielding one of my great weapons of course.
Brownbark is a woodcutter who lives somewhere in Ravenwood with his son, Anrak.
Bane Blackblood wants to rule over the island of Raven's Dust but he won't as "King" "Theodore" "XIII"'s guards are using my weapons. *smile*
I heard he won the throne by sleeping. I wish I could do the same.
He is the orc leader.
Althea is the name of the world in which you are.
Do not be afraid to come back to my shop if you need anything else.
Ask me about goblins if you're hunting a bounty. I keep count same as everyone else on this island does.

welcomeText: Careful past the ridge, friend. The Cinderreach Hills have been smoking worse than usual.

topics.response: Ashfang Stalkers have been raiding the foothills in packs, and they're bolder every week. Cull enough of them and there's coin in it for you.
There's a drake denned up in the hills, one the Stalkers answer to. Ignarok, the old maps call him. I wouldn't go looking for him without a good blade.
I've traded a few fire workings off travelers over the years. Ask to TEACH if you've got the coin and the nerve.
Cinderreach used to be good grazing land, south of Windhowl. Now half of it's scorched black and the other half is smoking.
Watch the wind - it carries the smoke, and worse. Safe travels.

welcomeText: Corwin here. If you're heading east past the fields, best prove you can handle yourself first.

topics.response: The antelope herds past the fields have turned skittish and mean since the tide started acting up east of town - something's spooked them. Thin their numbers and I'll know you can hold your own before you go looking for whatever's actually wrong out there.

There's an old shrine out past the coast east of here - the Sunken Chancel, folk call it. Something's been dragging people under since the tide 'woke' it. Not my business until it comes ashore, but it will, eventually.
Silversky's held the coast a long time. We don't send folk out past the fields without knowing they can handle themselves first - too many haven't come back.
Nothing wrong with antelope, normally. Lately they're jumpier and meaner than they should be - had one take a chunk out of a fisherman's arm last week.

welcomeText: Peace to you, traveler. This temple stands open to anyone the Veil has bruised, whichever side of the seam you call home.

topics.response: This temple sits at the seam on purpose. Neither the Wilds nor the Veil can claim consecrated ground.
The Wilds still sing, if you know how to listen. I pray it stays that way.
I have prayed over the Veil's dead more times than I can count. None of my prayers have slowed it. Go carefully if you must go there at all.

welcomeText: You hear the wyrmlings before you see them. If you can hear the Drake itself, you're already too close.

topics.response: Kraanian Wyrmlings have nested in the aerie east of here, and something far older sleeps above them. Thin the nest and I'll pay you from my own purse.
A true Drake hasn't been seen on this island in a generation. I've spent that long proving the old maps right.
Fly low, or don't fly at all. That's the only advice I have for you.
I can teach you Leyward Bastion, if you've the level and the mind for it - a ward that guards a whole party against the elements at once. Ask to TEACH.

welcomeText: Welcome. I have every spell known to this world for sale. Say "spells" to browse my wares.
The tide brought something foul ashore near Silversky. Stand with me, or move along.

topics.response: Drowned Acolytes have been crawling out of the flooded chancel east of town, dragging folk under the waves. Thin their numbers and I'll see you paid.
Mordrenn was a priest once, before the tide claimed him. Now he calls himself an Inquisitor and holds court in the drowned chancel, judging anyone who wades too close.
I picked up a working or two studying the tide magic that keeps those cultists breathing underwater. Ask to TEACH if you want to learn.
Silversky's coast used to be calm. Since the chancel woke up, the fishing fleets won't sail past the old lighthouse without an escort.
Safe travels. Keep your boots dry.

welcomeText: Don't linger past dusk here. The barrows wake at dark, and something crowned still walks among them.

topics.response: Wights have been crawling out of the old barrows south of the marches. Put them back down and I'll pay you from the March Watch's own coffer.
They call him the Hollow King. No one remembers which king he was in life. Whatever crowned him now isn't a kindness.
Keep your torch lit. It's the only mercy the barrows understand.

welcomeText: Bryndis, wayfarer and scroll-trader. Buy a Scroll of Avalon before you leave - you'll thank me the first time you need to get back here in a hurry.

topics.response: The Scroll of Avalon carries you straight to the Sanctuary temple, no matter how far you've wandered. Cheap insurance, if you ask me.
The Avalon Gateway is the spell woven into that scroll. Ask Archmage Thalindra if you'd rather learn to cast it yourself.
I don't sell passage into the Veil. Nobody sane charters that road on purpose.
